1.title: Wireless Devices and Technologies
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Wireless Devices and Technologies. It covers the exam area two point zero Network Implementation. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. two point three Given a scenario, select and configure wireless devices and technologies: channels, channel width, non-overlapping channels, regulatory impacts (eight oh two dot eleven H). Frequency options (two point four, five, six gigahertz, band steering). S S I D, B S S I D, E S S I D. Network types (mesh, ad hoc, point to point, infrastructure). Encryption (W P A two, W P A three). Guest networks and captive portals. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two point zero Network Implementation (twenty percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Frequencies and channels
1.text: Frequencies and channels. The figure shows this: The two point four gigahertz band with three non-overlapping channels, one, six and eleven.

1.title: Frequencies and channels, continued
1.text: Frequencies and channels. two point four gigahertz. Longer range, better wall penetration, slower and crowded; only three non-overlapping channels in the U S: one, six and eleven (twenty megahertz wide). five gigahertz. Faster, shorter range, many more non-overlapping channels; D F S channels need radar detection. six gigahertz. Newest (Wi-Fi six E and seven), very wide channels, little interference, shortest range, W P A three required. Channel width. Wider (forty, eighty, one hundred sixty megahertz) equals more speed but fewer free channels and more interference.

1.title: Frequencies and channels, continued
1.text: Frequencies and channels. Band steering. The A P or controller pushes dual-band clients to five gigahertz (or six gigahertz). Regulatory impact. Allowed channels and power differ by country; eight oh two dot eleven H adds dynamic frequency selection (D F S) and transmit power control to avoid radar. Exam tip: Use channels one, six and eleven at two point four gigahertz to avoid channel overlap between neighboring A P s.

1.title: SSIDs and network types
1.text: S S I Ds and network types. S S I D (service set identifier). The network name. B S S I D (basic service set identifier). The M A C address of one A P radio. E S S I D (extended service set identifier). One S S I D shared by several A P s for roaming. Infrastructure. Clients connect through an A P. Ad hoc (I B S S). Clients connect directly, no A P. Mesh. A P s relay traffic wirelessly to each other. Point to point. A wireless bridge between two sites with directional antennas.

1.title: Security and access
1.text: Security and access. W P A two. A E S-C C M P encryption; P S K (pre-shared key) for homes and small offices. W P A three. Stronger, S A E (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals) replaces P S K exchange, resists offline guessing, forward secrecy. P S K versus Enterprise. P S K: one shared passphrase. Enterprise: eight oh two dot one X with a R A D I U S server, each user has credentials. Guest network. Separate S S I D and V L A N with internet-only access and often a captive portal. Captive portal. A web page shown before access (terms, voucher, login). Exam tip: "Each employee signs in with their own credentials" equals W P A two or W P A three Enterprise (eight oh two dot one X and R A D I U S). "One shared passphrase" equals P S K.

1.title: Antennas and AP types
1.text: Antennas and A P types. Omnidirectional antenna. Radiates in all horizontal directions; general coverage. Directional antenna. Focuses a beam (Yagi, parabolic, patch): longer range, point to point. Autonomous A P. Configured and managed on its own. Lightweight A P. Managed by a wireless controller (for example over C A P W A P); central policy and roaming. Exam tip: W P A three uses S A E; W P A two Enterprise and W P A three Enterprise use eight oh two dot one X with R A D I U S. P S K is one shared passphrase.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Three neighboring access points at two point four gigahertz must avoid interfering with each other. Which channels should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: one, six and eleven. Channels one, six and eleven do not overlap.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company wants each employee to authenticate with unique credentials on Wi-Fi. Which setup fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: W P A three Enterprise with eight oh two dot one X and R A D I U S. Enterprise mode authenticates each user through R A D I U S.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A guest network should show a terms-of-use page before granting access. What is used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A captive portal. Captive portals present a web page before access.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which technology pushes dual-band clients toward the less crowded five gigahertz band? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Band steering. Band steering moves capable clients to five gigahertz.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A building-to-building link of two kilometers needs a focused wireless beam. Which antenna fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A directional antenna. Directional antennas focus the signal for long point-to-point links.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company manages eighty access points centrally with shared policy. Which A P type fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Lightweight access points with a controller. Lightweight A P s are managed by a controller.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the B S S I D? Answer: The M A C address of an A P radio. Question two. Name the three non-overlapping channels at two point four gigahertz. Answer: one, six and eleven. Question three. What does eight oh two dot eleven H add? Answer: D F S and transmit power control to avoid radar.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What replaces P S K key exchange in W P A three? Answer: S A E. Question five. What is an E S S I D? Answer: One S S I D shared by several access points. Question six. What does a captive portal do? Answer: Shows a web page before network access.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Bands: two point four gigahertz (range, one or six or eleven), five gigahertz (faster), six gigahertz (newest, W P A three). Names: S S I D (name), B S S I D (A P M A C), E S S I D (many A P s). Types: infrastructure, ad hoc, mesh, point to point. Security: W P A two (A E S-C C M P), W P A three (S A E); P S K versus Enterprise (eight oh two dot one X, R A D I U S); guest plus captive portal. Hardware: omni versus directional antennas; autonomous versus lightweight A P s.
